Articles

  • CBP rule: a foreign importer of record must use CTPAT validation or a CTPAT-validated licensed customs broker (FR 2026-22735, effective 2027-01-05)

    Verified 2026-11-17 · 中文

    From 2027-01-05 a foreign IOR must be CTPAT-validated or use a CTPAT-validated licensed customs broker, and a U.S. IOR declares its status on each entry. Key dates, who is affected, the options, and what the rule text does not answer.

  • IEEPA duty refunds: CAPE or the CIT

    Verified 2026-11-17 · 中文

    Two routes for IEEPA duty refunds: a CAPE declaration in ACE, or a protest and then the CIT. Who receives the refund, the key dates, the periods that may apply, and what to gather.

  • Exporting to the EU? Three rules your EU buyers will ask you about before 30 December 2026

    Updated 2026-10-10 · 中文

    The EU deforestation regulation applies to large and medium operators from 30 December 2026, the green-claims ban has applied since 27 September 2026, and the packaging regulation since 12 August 2026. What each one means for a Chinese factory or seller supplying the EU, what the EU buyer will ask for, and what to prepare.

  • Received a CBP Form 28 (CF-28)? What to Do Next

    Updated 2026-09-20

    A CBP Form 28 is a Request for Information about specific import entries. What it means, what to identify before you answer, which dates matter, what to keep, and when a broker or an attorney fits.
